commands.name: push
commands.summary: Upload files, get a link for each

flags.name: run
flags.usage: Attach to an existing run instead of opening one. Its slug, or a link carrying it

flags.name: caption
flags.usage: What this file shows, recorded on the artifact as `krowk.caption`. Repeat to caption several files, in the order they are given

flags.name: destination
flags.usage: Print what this tool wants pasted into it, e.g. github or slack. A tool krowk has not been told about gets the markdown block

flags.name: pull-request
flags.usage: Pull request the work belongs to

flags.name: link
flags.usage: Link this work is about — the issue, the spec, the discussion. An absolute http(s) URL, repeatable up to 20, recorded on the run as `krowk.links`

flags.name: link-title
flags.usage: What to call the --link before it, instead of its URL. One line

flags.name: link-rel
flags.usage: What the --link before it is: tracks, fixes, spec, discussion, source, supersedes — or a word of your own

flags.name: reference
flags.usage: Related identifier that is not a URL, e.g. a ticket key — repeat for more than one. A URL is a --link

flags.name: session
flags.usage: Agent session ID

flags.name: title
flags.usage: Title for the work this push belongs to, recorded on the run. What a pasted link says is the artifact's --caption

flags.name: repo
flags.usage: Override the detected repository

flags.name: commit
flags.usage: Override the detected commit

flags.name: agent
flags.usage: Override the detected agent

flags.name: metadata
flags.usage: Extra key=value metadata — your value wins over a detected one. Public

global_flags.name: workspace
global_flags.usage: Use this workspace's stored key for this one command — outranks KROWK_WORKSPACE and every config file

global_flags.name: dev
global_flags.usage: Talk to a local registry at http://localhost:8787/v1

global_flags.name: format
global_flags.usage: human | json | markdown | url (default: human on a TTY, json when piped)

global_flags.name: jq
global_flags.usage: Filter the JSON with a jq expression — built in, no jq binary needed. Implies --format json, and reads the bare record under --quiet

environment.name: KROWK_TOKEN
environment.usage: API token — wins over the credentials file

environment.name: KROWK_WORKSPACE
environment.usage: Workspace whose stored key to use, as if by --workspace — outranks the config files, loses to the flag

environment.name: KROWK_NO_UPDATE_CHECK
environment.usage: 1/true/yes/on — never check for or mention new releases
